title: Final Fantasy VII Almost Stayed a Nintendo Game
hook:
Final Fantasy VII started life as a Super Nintendo game in 1994, and Square only jumped to PlayStation because three CDs of game would never fit on a cartridge. Would you have picked cartridge or disc back then?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.

script: Did you know Final Fantasy Seven was almost a Nintendo game? Square started planning it in nineteen ninety four as a Super Nintendo game. Then the team started experimenting with Nintendo's next console, the Nintendo Sixty Four. In August of nineteen ninety five, Square showed a playable 3D demo at a computer graphics convention. It ran on Silicon Graphics workstations and starred Locke, Terra and Shadow from Final Fantasy Six. Then Nintendo chose cartridges for its new console instead of CDs. Square did the math and decided the game it wanted to make would never fit on a cartridge. Series creator Hironobu Sakaguchi later said PlayStation games being on CDs was the biggest factor. In January of nineteen ninety six, Square announced the game was moving to the Sony PlayStation. The finished game filled three CDs and sold more than ten million copies on the original PlayStation. The breakup was rough. Square's president said there were about four or five years where they could not really talk to Nintendo. The two companies did not patch things up until two thousand two, when Square agreed to make games for the GameCube and Game Boy Advance. Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles arrived the next year, the first Final Fantasy on a Nintendo console in a decade. Follow for more gaming history.
